title: Normalized rational and common-stage descent of point-section transformations
statement:
Fix the finite-field datum $p,a,q,k_0,k$ [def-weil-finite-field-fiber], a prime $\ell\ne p$, a chosen algebraic closure $\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell$, and all finite intermediate fields $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ with their valuation rings $\mathcal O_E$ and uniformizers [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension]. Put $s=\operatorname{Spec}k$, let $g:s\to s$ be any scheme automorphism [def-weil-scheme-morphism-properties], and use its small pro-etale site [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site]. Write $\mathcal C_E^{\mathrm{int}}=D^b_c(s,\mathcal O_E)$ for the derived-complete constructible category [def-weil-derived-complete-integral-detailed], $P_E=Lg_E^*$ for completed pullback and its rational and common-stage extensions [def-weil-derived-pullback-tensor-hom], and $F_E^{\mathrm{int}}=\Gamma(s,-)=\operatorname{Fib}_s$ [def-weil-finite-coefficient-point]. The objects $P_EK$ are again in $\mathcal C_E^{\mathrm{int}}$ [lem-weil-isomorphism-derived-pullback].

For every $E$ suppose given morphisms $\eta^E_K:F_E^{\mathrm{int}}K\to F_E^{\mathrm{int}}(P_EK)$ in $D(\mathcal O_E)$, natural for every morphism of $\mathcal C_E^{\mathrm{int}}$. For $E\subset L$, let $T_{L/E}$ be completed integral scalar extension [def-weil-integral-scalar-extension], $\alpha_K:T_{L/E}P_EK\xrightarrow{\sim}P_LT_{L/E}K$ the specified pullback comparison [lem-pur-integral-operations-scalar-extension], and $\varphi_K:F_L^{\mathrm{int}}(T_{L/E}K)\xrightarrow{\sim}F_E^{\mathrm{int}}K\otimes_{\mathcal O_E}\mathcal O_L$ the specified sections comparison [lem-weil-point-sections-scalar-extension]. Assume, under their identity and successive-extension identifications,
$$\varphi_{P_EK}F_L^{\mathrm{int}}(\alpha_K)^{-1}\eta^L_{T_{L/E}K}=(\eta^E_K\otimes1)\varphi_K.$$

On the raw rationalization $\mathcal C_E=D^b_c(s,E)$ [def-weil-rationalization-karoubi], set $F_E=\operatorname{Fib}_s$ with its specified action on morphism tensors, and $H_E=F_EP_E$. Then $\eta^{E,\mathrm{rat}}_K=\eta^E_K\otimes_{\mathcal O_E}E$ is natural for every morphism $u\in\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal C_E}(K,K')$, including arbitrary sums $u=\sum_jv_j\otimes a_j$, and is scalar-compatible under the rationalizations of exactly $\alpha,\varphi$ above.

More precisely, let $\bar\varphi_{E,L,K}:F_L(K\otimes_EL)\xrightarrow{\sim}F_EK\otimes_EL$ and $\bar\alpha_{E,L,K}:(P_EK)\otimes_EL\xrightarrow{\sim}P_L(K\otimes_EL)$ be those rational comparisons, and put
$$b_{E,L,K}=\bar\varphi_{E,L,P_EK}F_L(\bar\alpha_{E,L,K})^{-1}:H_L(K\otimes_EL)\xrightarrow{\sim}H_EK\otimes_EL.$$
On $D^b_c(s,\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell)$ [def-weil-algebraically-closed-coefficients], the components at $(E,K)$ represented by $\eta^{E,\mathrm{rat}}_K$ form a natural transformation from the specified point-fiber functor to its composite with $Lg^*$, with values in the common-stage point category [def-weil-point-fd-qlbar-category]. For a representative $u:K\otimes_EL\to K'\otimes_{E'}L$, the two functors act respectively by the classes of
$$\bar\varphi_{E',L,K'}F_L(u)\bar\varphi_{E,L,K}^{-1},\qquad b_{E',L,K'}H_L(u)b_{E,L,K}^{-1}.$$
Their naturality equation holds over this same $L$, with the component maps extended to $L$; it is preserved by further finite extension and gives the same equation for any equivalent common-stage representative. The assertion concerns arbitrary supplied integral transformations $\eta$, without prescribing their components.

source.place: Deligne, Weil II, (1.1.3), p. 150 and (1.1.7), pp. 150-151; explicit pro-etale/completed-coefficient argument extracted by Q97 from original steps 3-6 and 9 of lem-weil-frobenius-point-transport-natural. The normalized comparison and common-stage realization assertions are agent-written, not theorems asserted by Deligne.

proof.text: Use [lem-weil-isomorphism-derived-pullback] with the automorphism $g$ of $s$; $\ell$ is invertible since $\ell\ne p$. Thus $P_E$ preserves the integral category. By [def-weil-rationalization-karoubi] the rational category has exactly the integral objects and Hom groups tensored with $E$. The formulas in [def-weil-finite-coefficient-point] and [def-weil-derived-pullback-tensor-hom] give, for an integral $v:K\to K'$ and $a\in E$, $F_E(v\otimes a)=a(F_E^{\mathrm{int}}(v)\otimes E)$ and $H_E(v\otimes a)=a(F_E^{\mathrm{int}}(P_Ev)\otimes E)$. In particular the proposed component $t_{E,K}:=\eta^E_K\otimes E$ has source $F_EK$ and target $H_EK$, both in $D^b_{\mathrm{fd}}(E)$.

source.place: (1.1.3), p. 150: rational Hom tensors and finite-field coefficient colimit; explicit formal argument by Q93 using the normalized comparisons stated in the cited DAG nodes. (1.1.7), pp. 150-151 supplies the point-transport context only.

proof.text: For integral $v:K\to K'$, the assumed naturality is $F_E^{\mathrm{int}}(P_Ev)\eta^E_K=\eta^E_{K'}F_E^{\mathrm{int}}(v)$. Apply the module-complex scalar-extension functor $-\otimes_{\mathcal O_E}E$ and multiply the resulting equality by $a\in E$. The formulas of [def-weil-finite-coefficient-point] and [def-weil-derived-pullback-tensor-hom] give $H_E(v\otimes a)t_{E,K}=t_{E,K'}F_E(v\otimes a)$. Every tensor is a finite sum of pure tensors by [def-weil-rationalization-karoubi]. Bilinearity of composition therefore gives, for $u=\sum_jv_j\otimes a_j$, $H_E(u)t_{E,K}=\sum_j a_j(H_E(v_j\otimes1)t_{E,K})=\sum_j a_j(t_{E,K'}F_E(v_j\otimes1))=t_{E,K'}F_E(u)$. This includes zero, sums and every balanced tensor representative, since both functor maps already factor through the tensor product.

proof.text:
For $E\subset L$, tensor the assumed integral compatibility equation with $L$ over $\mathcal O_L$. The last display of [lem-weil-point-sections-scalar-extension] identifies its sections comparisons with precisely $\bar\varphi_{E,L}$, and rationalizing the pullback comparison of [lem-pur-integral-operations-scalar-extension] gives precisely $\bar\alpha_{E,L}$. Consequently the equation becomes
$$b_{E,L,K}\,t_{L,K\otimes_E L}=(t_{E,K}\otimes_E L)\,\bar\varphi_{E,L,K}. \tag{*}$$
No comparison is replaced by an arbitrary isomorphism: tensoring is a functor, so it preserves the composite and the inverse occurring in the supplied equation. Tensoring the unit and tower equations in the two cited statements preserves those equations too. This proves the specified rational scalar compatibility, including equality of fields.

proof.text:
Write $S_{L/E}K=K\otimes_E L$, $T_{L/E}A=A\otimes_E L$, and write $a^C:S_{N/L}S_{L/E}\xrightarrow{\sim}S_{N/E}$ and $a^D:T_{N/L}T_{L/E}\xrightarrow{\sim}T_{N/E}$ for the specified associators. For $E\subset L\subset N$, suppress these associators momentarily. The two cited tower equations read
$$\bar\alpha_{E,N}=\bar\alpha_{L,N,S_{L/E}K}\,S_{N/L}(\bar\alpha_{E,L}),\qquad \bar\varphi_{E,N}=(\bar\varphi_{E,L}\otimes_LN)\bar\varphi_{L,N,S_{L/E}K}.$$
Insert these expressions into $b_{E,N}=\bar\varphi_{E,N,P_EK}F_N(\bar\alpha_{E,N})^{-1}$ and use naturality of $\bar\varphi_{L,N}$ for $\bar\alpha_{E,L}^{-1}$. The result, with associators restored, is
$$b_{E,N,K}H_N(a^C_K)=a^D_{H_EK}(b_{E,L,K}\otimes_LN)b_{L,N,S_{L/E}K}. \tag{**}$$
Explicitly the middle interchange is $\bar\varphi_{L,N,S_{L/E}P_EK}F_N(S_{N/L}\bar\alpha_{E,L}^{-1})=(F_L(\bar\alpha_{E,L}^{-1})\otimes_LN)\bar\varphi_{L,N,P_LS_{L/E}K}$. This gives (**), and the unit equations give $b_{E,E}=1$ under unit identifications. Naturality follows by composing the two natural isomorphisms defining $b$. All the inputs here are the naturality, identity and tower assertions of [lem-weil-point-sections-scalar-extension] and [lem-pur-integral-operations-scalar-extension].

proof.text: Let $u:S_{L/E}K\to S_{L/E'}K'$ represent a common-stage arrow as in [def-weil-algebraically-closed-coefficients]. The point-fiber action in [def-weil-finite-coefficient-point] is $A_L(u)=\bar\varphi_{E',L,K'}F_L(u)\bar\varphi_{E,L,K}^{-1}$. The pullback action of [def-weil-derived-pullback-tensor-hom] first gives $\bar\alpha_{E',L,K'}^{-1}P_L(u)\bar\alpha_{E,L,K}$. Apply the point-fiber action to this arrow, now between $P_EK$ and $P_{E'}K'$. Expanding $F_L$ of the composite gives exactly $B_L(u)=b_{E',L,K'}H_L(u)b_{E,L,K}^{-1}$. Thus these are the two specified functors, rather than alternative realizations. At a common stage they preserve identities and composition: the intermediate $\bar\varphi^{-1}\bar\varphi$ or $b^{-1}b$ cancels, and $F_L,H_L$ are functors. The two tower equations (the sections equation and (**)) show that scalar extension of $A_L(u),B_L(u)$ is respectively $A_N(u_N),B_N(u_N)$ after the source and target associators. Hence their classes are unchanged by further extension, and by changing to any equivalent representative, using the equality criterion of [def-weil-point-fd-qlbar-category].

source.place: (1.1.3), p. 150: rational Hom tensors and finite-field coefficient colimit; explicit formal argument by Q93 using the normalized comparisons stated in the cited DAG nodes. (1.1.7), pp. 150-151 supplies the point-transport context only.

proof.text:
The proposed component at $(E,K)$ is the finite-stage class of $t_{E,K}$. Put $t^L_{E,K}=t_{E,K}\otimes_E L$ with the target-category unit identifications of [def-weil-point-fd-qlbar-category]. Equation (*) says $b_{E,L,K}^{-1}t^L_{E,K}=t_{L,S_{L/E}K}\bar\varphi_{E,L,K}^{-1}$. Apply Step 2 at field $L$ to the arbitrary rational morphism $u:S_{L/E}K\to S_{L/E'}K'$ and calculate in $D(L)$:
$$\begin{aligned} B_L(u)t^L_{E,K}&=b_{E',L,K'}H_L(u)t_{L,S_{L/E}K}\bar\varphi_{E,L,K}^{-1}\\ &=b_{E',L,K'}t_{L,S_{L/E'}K'}F_L(u)\bar\varphi_{E,L,K}^{-1}\\ &=t^L_{E',K'}\bar\varphi_{E',L,K'}F_L(u)\bar\varphi_{E,L,K}^{-1}=t^L_{E',K'}A_L(u).\end{aligned}$$
This is naturality over the very same field $L$, before passing to any colimit.

proof.text: For a further finite field $N\supset L$, apply $-\otimes_LN$ to the equality of Step 6 and conjugate by the source and target tower associators. Functoriality preserves the equality and the expansions of Step 5 identify it with the equation for $u_N$. If $[L,u]=[L',v]$, [def-weil-algebraically-closed-coefficients] gives $N\supset L,L'$ with $u_N=v_N$. The two equations then have identical sides in $D(N)$; by [def-weil-point-fd-qlbar-category] they yield the same equality of morphism classes. Therefore all supplied integral components give the claimed natural transformation on the common-stage category. This proves independence of representative without assuming injectivity of transition maps, invertibility of $\eta$, or any special formula for its components.
